articles.title: Ronaldo finally reveals 'the truth' he promised, details Jorge Jesus’ betrayal in damning statement and vows to return
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo reveals the real reasons for his departure from the Portugal national team, detailing a betrayal by coach Jorge Jesus. Find out all the shocking details in his lengthy statement.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has finally explained why he walked away from the Portugal camp, delivering the detailed account he promised when the dispute with Jorge Jesus first erupted. The 41-year-old had said he would tell the Portuguese people what really happened “in due time”, and that moment has now arrived, with Ronaldo setting out the conversations that preceded his departure, the promises he says were made to him, the press conference that changed everything and the reasons he ultimately decided to leave.Ronaldo had played in Portugal's 1-0 Nations League victory over Wales before becoming an unused substitute in the following 2-1 win against Norway, despite warming up for around 30 minutes. Jesus later explained that he had considered bringing Ronaldo onto the pitch but decided against it, while an emergency meeting involving Ronaldo, the Portugal coach and Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proença took place afterwards.That meeting did not settle the dispute, and Ronaldo left the Portugal camp ahead of the team's 4-2 victory against Denmark. At the time, he issued a short statement saying that he would eventually reveal the reasons behind his decision, while Portugal continued their campaign without him and went on to win all four of their Nations League matches, taking 12 points from 12 and becoming the first team to secure qualification for the quarter-finals.Jesus subsequently gave his own account after Portugal's 2-1 victory over Norway, saying Ronaldo remained eligible for selection and that the decision over whether he returned belonged entirely to the player.Ronaldo has now provided his version of events in a lengthy statement posted across his social media channels, taking the story from the aftermath of the 2026 World Cup through to his decision to leave the Portugal camp. The statement comes with Ronaldo back at Al-Nassr, where he has already returned to training following his departure from the national team and is preparing to resume club football.Ronaldo's full statement"As I promised, I have decided to recount, in the first person and directly, the circumstances surrounding the latest stage of the national team's journey.After the 2026 World Cup, I prepared a message for the Portuguese people, which I still keep, containing the words I would like to address to them when I finally leave our team.At the end of the tournament, on the return flight from the United States, the federation president asked me and insisted that I reconsider my decision to leave, because the Portuguese Football Federation wished for me to continue.Immediately afterwards, he asked me for my opinion on the name of the current national team coach, whom he was considering, alongside other names he did not reveal to me.I answered the federation president that, in my opinion, it would be the ideal choice. Therefore, on the day the current national team coach was presented, I was genuinely happy with this choice. It was the right choice, as the results prove.A few days later, I received the first call from the new national team coach, in which he said he wished to meet me in person. I answered in the affirmative, and we set a date for it. "The end of my holiday."We met at the football city where my team was holding its pre-season training camp.On that day the coach told me that he was counting on me and that my presence was essential to his project. He presented me with a plan for my immediate participation. He said I would play the first and last matches, and that he would make three or four changes in each match for reasons related to physical fitness.At that point, he suggested that I not travel with the national team to Norway and Denmark. He suggested that I play the first match and stay in Portugal, then join them before the match at the Dragão stadium.I rejected this suggestion immediately. It seemed clear to me that I could not accept it. Not playing the matches abroad would not mean that I would not be captain of our team. The privilege of staying in Portugal would not set a good example.In the end, the coach agreed with my analysis.This conversation was attended by Simo Coutinho, the sporting director of Al-Nassr club, the person to whom the current national team coach reported throughout last season, and one of those responsible for his joining the club in 2025.On the eve of the training camp, the coach came to my home in Lisbon to have another conversation with me at his request. The conversation was calm, and we adhered to all the principles agreed upon in August. I played the match at the Alvalade stadium, and despite being substituted, I caused no problems. I personally placed the captain's armband on Bruno Fernandes, and it never occurred to me that I might be taking my last steps as a player and captain of the national team. The most important thing that day, for me, was our win. Winning is always a good thing, and in Portugal, and for my country, it is the best.At lunchtime on the day of the match in Norway, the national team coach's assistant came to the table where the team was having lunch, and told me that the coach wanted to talk to me. To my great surprise, the coach asked me whether I was ready to play 30 minutes. I was fully focused on my physical recovery, blending in with my teammates as usual, and believing I would not play that day. No problem at all.This request was outside my physical recovery and training plan, because I was only going to play on the fourth of the month at the Dragão stadium, but of course I agreed. He answered me that I should be ready because I would play 30 minutes.The rest is well known. I began warming up from half-time, and I watched the minutes pass, and no one called me on. The coach broke his promise.At the end of the match, I only wanted everything to end with a win and to be alone. I did not go to greet the fans. A mistake I take responsibility for alone, and one that should not have happened. I apologise to the Portuguese people who supported us enthusiastically there, I apologise to the fans, and I apologise to those who travelled there to see me, even if they were not Portuguese, and whom I may have let down.Forty-eight hours later, we had a conversation, myself, the coach and Simo Coutinho, because he was following our conversationsIt was a very deep and frank moment, without any reservation.We agreed that there was only one way to end this "case": that the coach would repeat what he had just told me in private, in the presence of Simo Coutinho, but in the press conference room.The agreement was simple: the coach would begin the press conference with this subject, trying to end the matter by telling the truth. He would say that I had never asked to play even for a few minutes, and that the coach alone, no one else, was the one who proposed the plan for this training camp, and that it had been a mistake to subject me only to the warm-up without playing, and that, if it happened again, he would not do it.We ended that meeting with the coach asking me for a hug, and he promised me that he would say in the press conference what he had just told me, and that the matter had been resolved. I would not play in Denmark, but I would play in the Dragão match. All of this took place in the presence of Simo Coutinho, as usual.At the coach's request, a video meeting was held between him, Simo Coutinho and Tiago Craveiro, to summarise what we had discussed.A brief document was prepared, which I personally approved, and it was handed to the coach at his request.The meeting was as expected: the behaviour had nothing to do with our meeting. I heard expressions and aggression that I consider unjustified, and an attitude suggesting that he "wants, can, and orders" that he had never shown me, not even indirectly, in a private session, the day before.The notes I reviewed were as follows: I believe it is important, because it is the truth, to clarify some matters before talking about Denmark:I personally proposed a plan for Cristiano, without anyone else, for this sporting season with the national team. It was a long and very fruitful conversation.I know how much he loves the national team and his global standing, and more than that, how positive his influence has been on the national team over 24 consecutive years.The plan I proposed to Cristiano was accepted.He never questioned my choices. He was an example to be followed, loyal, and professional.The Norway match was not included in the plan I had set for him. However, I felt that he had physically recovered from the first match, and I warned him that I might be forced to bring him on. Cristiano agreed.I made a mistake by involving a player of the magnitude of Pelé or Maradona only in the warm-up without involving him in the match. If it were today, I would not do that.In short: I want Cristiano in the national team. In truth, I do not want a little, I want a lot. And fortunately, he also trusts me. He believed in me at Al-Nassr and here too.As for not greeting the fans, we spoke about this matter earlier. A player who has played more than 230 matches with the national team does not take lessons from me in loving Portugal. It was a moment of frustration that erases nothing. He is the player who signs the most, takes the most selfies, and shows the most affection to the fans. Let us not create problems out of nothing. When we are not happy, we react. That is all there is to it. None of these notes, therefore, mentioned that the coach had apologised to me.This was the second time he broke his promise.I decided to leave the training camp without waiting for another promise that would not be kept. For me, the truth remains the most important thing in relationships between people. However painful it may be, I want the truth to be told to me.In fact, in a conversation I had with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation and the coach on the morning of that press conference, you can verify this, I assured them that if they did not want my presence, they should tell me so. They only had to be frank with me. I would have accepted it and promised them that we would prepare something wonderful, as I hope will happen, and no one would be angry.I remember it as if it happened yesterday. They answered with one voice in unison. assuring that my place is in the national team.I have never intervened, at any time, in any technical or tactical decision of any coach or national team official throughout nearly 25 years of my career. I accept, whether it is good or bad, what they propose. I respect the decision, and when they break their promise to me, I feel that my place is not here.I also apologise to my national team teammates for leaving the training camp. For despite my complete breach of the coach's trust, as everyone who witnessed these conversations can attest, I should not have done that. The responsibility rests on me alone.I apologise to the Portuguese people once again, but the breaking of my promise had a profound effect on me. I felt that my continuing with the team, from that moment, would only harm it, so I did what I always said I would do if I did not feel I was of use: I packed my bags and left.The Portuguese Football Federation must assess the consequences of my actions and punish me for them. I believe the penalty should not be reduced. I am not just an ordinary player; I am the captain of the team, and that is an aggravating factor. I have already apologised, but I know that actions have consequences. Anyone in the world of football, like me, knows that the rules are the same for everyone, regardless of individual standing.In this regard, I have heard a lot about farewell matches, and that I need a farewell befitting me, and that the federation wishes to grant me this opportunity.I learned in life, while suffering from hunger and having nothing to eat, that no one gives anything to anyone for free. I can promise all my fans, and especially the Portuguese people, that we will play one or more farewell matches; there will be time for that.But when I think of the national team, what I really think of is competition. That is what I thought of on the day I received the news of my father's death. I was at a training camp with our national team, and I decided to stay there until the end of the next day's match. I did for my country what I would never have done for any club.So, if I am physically fit, playing for my club and, hopefully, scoring goals, after serving whatever suspension that will be imposed on me, I will be available, as I always have been, to compete and win with our national team.This, believe me, is the absolute truth."Cristiano Ronaldo,6 October 2026Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cucurella hace otro país 'enemigo'
articles.standfirst: El lateral español vuelve a ser señalado por una grada rival, esta vez tras la expulsión de Perisic por una falta sobre él
articles.summary: El lateral español vuelve a ser señalado por una grada rival, esta vez tras la expulsión de Perisic por una falta sobre él
articles.body: Cucurella tiene un problema con las gradas. O, mejor dicho, hay gradas que tienen un problema con Cucurella. Lo que empezó en Alemania después de aquella mano en la Eurocopa ha ido dejando capítulos por el camino y ahora ha encontrado un nuevo escenario: Croacia. En Split, el lateral español volvió a escuchar los pitos cada vez que entraba en contacto con el balón. Y esta vez la situación tuvo una particularidad... ya que la acción que encendió todavía más a la grada ni siquiera fue culpa suya. Minuto 79. Ivan Perisic persigue a Cucurella y acaba cazándolo por detrás cuando el lateral español se marcha en carrera. Falta y segunda amarilla para el croata. Hubo revisión, pero no había nada que cambiar: el contacto existió y Perisic recibió la segunda cartulina. Un minuto después, Croacia se quedaba con diez. Cucurella, mientras tanto, se llevaba los pitos. ¿Qué culpa tendrá él? Ninguna. Fue Perisic quien llegó tarde en una acción en la que nunca tuvo que entrar. Le trabó por detrás, seguramente no fuese su intención, y fue el árbitro quien decidió mostrarle la segunda amarilla. Cucurella simplemente estaba allí. Y todo empezó hace más de dos años. "Yo creo que es clara, hay contacto, segunda amarilla y nada que objetar, ellos tienen que defender a su equipo, nos han puesto las cosas muy difíciles pero hay que quedarse con la reacción del partido, quizás hemos empezado dormidos", aseguró tras el partido. Cuartos de final de la Eurocopa. España y Alemania se juegan el pase a semifinales y, con el partido en la prórroga con 1-1 en el marcador, apareció de la nada una jugada que cambiaría para siempre la relación de Cucurella con el fútbol alemán. Musiala disparó desde la frontal y el balón golpeó en la mano del lateral español dentro del área. Un posible penalti que Anthony Taylor no señaló... y Mikel Merino hizo el resto. Un año después, Cucurella volvió a jugar en Alemania en la 'Final Four' de la Nations League. Esta vez en el Allianz Arena, en la semifinal contra Francia. Y la grada, que era mayoría alemana, no había olvidado aquella mano. "Creo que me van a volver a pitar, pero estoy preparado. Yo no hice nada malo, no dependió de mí", aseguró antes el lateral. Sin embargo, la historia se repitió casi un año después. El lateral estrenaba camiseta con el Real Madrid en un amistoso contra el Schalke. Entró en el minuto 61 y la grada del Veltins-Arena volvió a recibirle con una sonora pitada. Y ahora aparece Croacia.

articles.title: El Güímar-Sporting Hortaleza se jugará a puerta cerrada en Tenerife

articles.summary: El duelo suspendido se disputará el domingo a las 12.00 hora insular (13.00 en la península)
articles.body: Ya hay resolución para uno de los grandes jaleos de la temporada. El partido de Atlético Unión Güímar y el Sporting Hortaleza que da acceso a jugar contra el Sevilla en la Copa del Rey se disputará el domingo 11 de octubre... en Tenerife. El Juez Único de Competiciones No Profesionales resuelve "la celebración en terreno neutral y a puerta cerrada del encuentro suspendido, Atlético Unión Güimar – AD Sporting Hortaleza, de vuelta de la eliminatoria previa del campeonato de España / Copa de S.M. El Rey, el próximo domingo 11 de octubre de 2026, a las 12:00 horas, hora insular, en el campo de fútbol El Peñón de Puerto de la Cruz (Tenerife)". Llama la atención que el duelo se juegue en campo neutral, pero en Tenerife, permitiendo el desplazamiento de los aficionados del Güímar a la zona del encuentro, a 45 minutos en coche de la localidad tinerfeña. La resolución explica la decisión: "La celebración en un terreno neutral permite situar el encuentro en un escenario distinto de aquel en el que se produjeron los incidentes, mientras que su celebración a puerta cerrada debería contribuir a reducir el riesgo de producción de nuevos episodios de amenazas, intimidación o violencia relacionados con la presencia de espectadores. Ambas medidas resultan complementarias y proporcionadas a las circunstancias excepcionales de este caso y tienen como única finalidad posibilitar que la eliminatoria se pueda celebrar con las debidas garantías para sus participantes". Los altercados en la previa del partido (petardos, pedradas al bus visitante, insulto e incluso lanzamientos de botellas y puñetazos) provocaron la decisión del equipo madrileño de no jugar el partido. En el acta, el colegiado explicó que "tras 37 minutos de retraso, se persona el dispositivo de la Guardia Civil: "El teniente nos confirma que la seguridad está garantizada durante todo el encuentro, y le trasladamos nuestra confianza en el dispositivo". Una teoría que ha defendido en todo momento el equipo canario, pero no el madrileño: "D. Luis Martínez Urquiza nos comunica de forma clara que, tras hablar con la directiva, el cuerpo técnico y los jugadores, el Sporting Hortaleza no quiere disputar el encuentro. Los motivos que alega son las circunstancias vividas tanto a su llegada al campo como durante la previa a la salida al terreno de juego, hechos que le han llevado a que emocionalmente no estén preparados para jugar".

articles.title: Dylan Stewart Returns to South Carolina Practice After Suspension for Punching Alabama Player
articles.summary: South Carolina pass-rusher Dylan Stewart returned to practice Tuesday following his one-game suspension, but it remains to be seen whether he will play in Saturday's contest against Florida.
articles.body:
South Carolina pass-rusher Dylan Stewart returned to practice Tuesday following his one-game suspension, but it remains to be seen whether he will play in Saturday's contest against Florida.

"He was at practice today," Gamecocks head coach Shane Beamer told reporters . "His status for Saturday has not been determined. That will be determined as we go throughout the week."

The SEC and South Carolina jointly suspended Stewart for the team's game against Kentucky after he punched a player during a loss to Alabama. The SEC's announcement said the punishment was "for egregious contact against an opposing player."

Stewart would be in line for a more severe punishment if there are any other issues.

"Dylan Stewart's egregious contact reflects behavior that is unacceptable and not aligned with the standards of the Southeastern Conference," SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey said when issuing the suspension. "Such action against an opponent carries a serious risk of injury and has no place in our conference competition. This suspension is appropriate, and any future misconduct by Dylan Stewart will result in more severe disciplinary action."

In addition to punching a player, Stewart appeared to be frustrated with his own team's coaching staff as he was being substituted out:

South Carolina's defense struggled without its star pass-rusher on the field during a 35-34 loss to Kentucky. Wildcats quarterback Kenny Minchey threw for three touchdowns and connected with Willie Rodriguez for the winning two-point conversion following the final touchdown.

The Gamecocks are now 2-3 overall and 0-3 in SEC play following a third consecutive loss. They were far more competitive against UK than they were during a 49-18 defeat to the Crimson Tide, but it was still another setback for a program looking to bounce back from last year's 4-8 mark.

As for Stewart, he is widely considered one of the best defensive prospects in the sport.

B/R's NFL Scouting Department ranked him as the fifth-best overall player in its latest big board of prospects for the 2027 NFL draft. It also listed him as the second-best edge-rusher and best speed-rusher in the class.

There is going to be additional attention on him because of his draft outlook, especially when he does return to the field following his suspension.

articles.title: Merino scores twice as Spain beat Croatia 2-1 in Nations League
articles.summary: Mikel Merino turns game for Spain in Croatia to maintain their 100 percent group-stage record in UEFA Nations League.
articles.body:
Mikel Merino hit a brace to help World Cup winners Spain seal qualification in the Nations League quarter-finals with a 2-1 win against Croatia on Tuesday.

Ivan Perisic put hosts Croatia ahead but substitute Merino equalised for Spain early in the second half.

Perisic was sent off with 10 minutes remaining for a second yellow card and Merino helped Spain capitalise with a fine finish to reach the last eight with two matches to spare.

Spain now has 42nd consecutive games without suffering defeat and lead England by three points at the top of Group A3.

Slaven Bilic’s Croatia were crushed 7-0 by England on Saturday, in front of a crowd of children as home fans were banned for racism, and came out determined to make it up to their supporters in Split.

Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon was called into action early on, saving well from Josip Stanisic’s header, as Luka Modric’s team impressed in the first half.

A few minutes later the hosts took the lead in Split with Simon saving from Igor Matanovic’s shot but Perisic reacted quickest to head home the rebound.

Athletic Bilbao goalkeeper Simon put Aymeric Laporte in a tough spot in his own box with a loose pass and Croatia intercepted and almost grabbed a second. However Simon saved from Freiburg striker Matanovic’s effort.

Spain’s teenage star Lamine Yamal raced through on goal early in the second half but he fell after nudging the ball past Barca team-mate and Croatia goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic.

Merino, on at the interval, pulled Spain level in the 61st minute with a low finish after Dani Olmo, who developed in Croatia as a youngster, fed him.

Croatia’s task of holding on in the final stages became harder when Perisic brought down Marc Cucurella and was dismissed.

Merino, so often making key impacts from the bench for Spain coach Luis De la Fuente, including in the World Cup this summer, finished the job with his second of the night.

The former Real Sociedad man, with two minutes remaining, produced a superb turn and finish to blast past Livakovic.

articles.title: Mikel Merino, el valor del antidivo
articles.summary: Al otro lado del espejo
articles.body: Cuatro partidos, cuatro victorias y hasta noviembre, cuando tocará visitar a Chequia (12) y recibir a Inglaterra (15). Como pasan dos, ya estamos clasificados. Si como campeones o no lo sabremos en su día. La victoria en Londres nos da ventaja, claro. De los cuatro partidos, el que más ha costado ha sido justamente el que acaba de terminar en Split cuando empiezo a escribir esto. Croacia venía de un estrepitoso 0-7 ante Inglaterra, pese a lo cual Bilic no dio un vuelco al equipo, apenas un par de cambios. Pero la colocación en el campo y la actitud fueron muy distintas. Se cerraron con firmeza, desconectando a Olmo, Pedri y Baena. Entre eso y que Oyarzabal estaba atrapado en la red y Rodri extrañamente confuso, allí sólo quedaba lo que hiciera Lamine, que insistió mucho sin cooperación. Pero es que además Croacia supo salir, apoyada en el buen juego de Modric, el recorrido de Kovacevic y la tremenda categoría de Perisic. Llegó bastante y con peligro. Unai sólo concedió un gol y podemos decir que en esa mala primera parte nuestra sostuvo el resultado en un límite digno. España empezó a encontrarse antes del descanso, según se le iban gastando las pilas a Croacia, y en la segunda parte por fin impuso su juego. Dominio muy completo y llegadas frecuentes, pero el gol no entraba hasta que apareció Merino, ese suplente providencial que ya ha acumulado un importante número de tantos decisivos. Este martes hizo los dos, el primero cruzando con serenidad, el segundo con un control extraordinario en postura difícil seguido de un tirazo a la escuadra que dejó a los croatas sin el consuelo de un empate que quizá hubieran merecido. Merino, jugador de físico potente y aire algo anticuado, que recuerda a los contumaces arietes que producían y exportaban los equipos del Norte de los años sesenta, es un tipo de estupenda técnica e inteligencia sutil para filtrarse en el área. Pero además es un modelo de la forma de estar en una plantilla, en este caso la de la selección, sin más ánimo ni objetivo que contribuir al bien común. Un suplente siempre a punto. No todos lo saben llevar así.

articles.title: Bilic: "¿Quién no está enfadado con Cucurella si no es de su equipo?"
articles.standfirst: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador croata tras el partido contra España
articles.summary: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador croata tras el partido contra España
articles.body: Slaven Bilic regresaba con la selección croata a Split, su ciudad natal. Después del enorme golpe del 0-7 en Rijeka ante Inglaterra el foco del partido ante España apuntaba directamente a él. Acaba de pasar por la sala de prensa del estadio del Hajduk para analizar el partido ante la campeona del mundo. Partido: "Hemos jugado muy bien. Siento el resultado. Un punto era mucho para nosotros. Se he hecho todo lo que preparamos, todo lo que trabajamos en la oscucridad. Estoy contento, en especial en la primera parte". Negatividad: "Me hace feliz el juego, la valentía. Ellos son mejores, pero en la primera parte hicimos mejores ocasiones. En la segunda notamos el desgaste físico. Además de que hemos tenido un proceso vírico de catrarro que nos ha afetcado a todos. Estoy orgulloso. En una ventana de dos partidos hubiese sido genial. Hay que tomar nota. Lo de Inglaterra no se va a olvidad nunca. Al menos a mí. Si alguien no lo ve así es mejor que no vuelva. Nadie nos tiene que explica qué supone esa derrota. La vergüenza que hemos pasado ahí queda. Ha sido muy duro". Cambio de plan de juego: "Jakic ha hecho lo que esperaba. No tengo dudas con él. Es valiente, sabe interpretar el juego. El problema es que en su club juega poco. Tiene esa energía que tanto necesitamos". Banquillos: "Había tensión, cosas de fútbol. He ido al vestuario a darles la enhorabuena. España es la campeona, pero tiene cositas de provocación. Como la tarjeta roja. Nada más". Cucurella: "¿Quién no está enfadado con Cucurella si no es de su equipo? Es un gra jugador, le admiro, por lo que hace en su campo y por la historia de su hijo. Defiende a su equipo con todo, pero claro que provoca". España: "No tiene debilidades. No hay un punto extacto que les puedas atacar. Pero el equipo perfecto no existe. Fuimos capaces de presionar bien y generarles problemas. Más que Inglaterra".

articles.title: Mikel Merino: "Ha habido alguna broma porque un compañero siempre me dice que solo meto de primer toque"

articles.body: El protagonista de la victoria ante Croacia fue una vez más Mikel Merino. El jugador del Arsenal ingresó en el terreno de juego en la segunda parte y fue el autor de los dos goles que valieron la remontada ante el conjunto arlequinado y posteriormente analizó el partido en zona mixta. Sobre su acierto goleador: Estoy contento de que últimamente me esté tocando acertar y como tú dices, que esta vez me haya valido para dar la vuelta a banderín. Siempre no los marco, va a llegar un día en el que no los meta y que no sea extraño". Protagonismo como suplente: "Es muy complicado salir al partido y generar un impacto con goles. Estoy teniendo la fortuna de que me están cayendo, estoy donde tengo que estar, lo estoy viviendo y me creo que puedo aportar al equipo". Secreto de sus goles: "El secreto viene siendo ese, no hay más que ambición, quererlo y quererlo y cuando te cae, estar preparado y haberlo entrenado". Firma ser suplente y marcar siempre: "A mí lo que me gusta es jugar al fútbol, entonces ser suplente siempre no es el mayor agrado para un futbolista. Estar en el campo es lo que me hace feliz, poder entrenar con mis compañeros y sentirme realizado con mi profesión. Por supuesto que salir del banquillo y meter gol te da una sensación espectacular, porque sobre todo si ayudas al equipo a ganar es único. No lo firmo, pero estoy contento por ello". El segundo gol: "Ha habido alguna broma que otra, porque un compañero siempre me dice que solo meto de primer toque y por fin meto uno de más de un toque. Ha sido justo cuando hemos cambiado un poquito el sistema (1:23) y me han retrasado un poquito la posición a número 8, pero sigo teniendo ese instinto llegador. (1:29) En cuanto he visto que llegaba el balón a Zubi con el pie abierto y sé la calidad que tiene para poner esos chips por encima de la última línea, me he desmarcado la espalda de ellos. Ha sido luego cuestión de intentar y controlar como pudiera. Se me ha quedado el balón perfecto después del control y finalizar arriba".

articles.title: Republic of Ireland U21s 3-1 England U21s: Lee Carsley's side suffer defeat in Cork as Ireland secure play-off place for Euro 2027
articles.summary: Match report as England U21s suffered a 3-1 defeat to the Republic of Ireland, who have now earned a play-off place for European Championship qualification; Lee Carsley's side have already qualified; the loss marked their only defeat of the qualifying campaign
articles.body:
Lee Carsley's men had already qualified for Euro 2027 as Group D winners but Ireland were competing for a play-off place, which they successfully secured when their deserved victory at Turner's Cross clinched second place at the expense of Slovakia on head-to-head record.

It was England's only defeat of their qualifying campaign and they paid the price for their defensive frailties, even though the early signs were promising.

They took the lead in the eighth minute when Divin Mubama's shot deflected across the face of goal and fell to Tyler Dibling, who hit the target with his first touch.

Some of the energy drained from their play, however, and in the 22nd minute a defensive lapse invited Ireland in for their opener.

The ball was played out to Sydie Peck but he was caught in possession and Ireland reacted to the opportunity in a flash, Rory Finneran passing to Lonergan who picked his spot and delivered a cool finish.

The home side then took the lead when Conor McManus tucked the ball home at the near post after Trent Koné-Doherty had been allowed to maraud free down the left touchline.

Koné-Doherty continued to cause problems with England slow to shut him down, but Carsley's men went desperately close shortly before half-time when Mubama was kept out by Noah Jauny.

Ireland were growing in confidence while their opponents became increasingly flat and they surged 3-1 ahead in the 63rd minute when Lonergan added his second following a scrappy passage of play in the box.

Once again England had been slow to react but in the 72nd minute they were denied by the post when Will Lankshear pulled the trigger amid a late onslaught that also saw Tyrique George kept out by a brilliant save from Jauny.

articles.title: Miami Hurricanes coach comes out in favor of ending preseason college football polls, blasts SEC
articles.summary: Shannon Dawson calls preseason rankings "the stupidest thing on the planet" and argues SEC teams get undeserved benefit of the doubt from voters.
articles.body: There may not be a better season than 2026 to exemplify the problems with preseason polls in college football. The advent of NIL and the transfer portal has already made gauging the "best" teams in early August nearly impossible, and as the jaw-dropping 2025 Indiana Hoosiers championship season demonstrated, the modern era has created more surprise teams than in the past. Preseason polls then, despite being a part of the college football process for years, are less useful than ever before. And one prominent offensive coordinator thinks we should get rid of them entirely. He's probably right. Miami Hurricanes OC Shannon Dawson recently addressed the preseason polls, specifically addressing how they consistently seemingly favor one specific conference. A conference that already more often than not gets the benefit of the doubt from poll voters. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "First of all, there should be no such thing as preseason rankings," Dawson said during a press conference. "That’s the most ridiculous thing on the planet. That is the stupidest thing, because people weigh those things way heavier than they should. "You shouldn’t have a ranking until October. How do you know? (Texas) A&M was ranked in the top-five, but how does that look right now? If anything, it isn’t predictable for the future, it’s the past. Go look at the top-10 last year. I did. Five of them weren’t even in the (end of season) top-25." It's impossible to argue with that, because it's true. And despite A&M, and others, looking far worse than their preseason expectations, the first few weeks of games and rankings reflect that initial set. Texas A&M loses to LSU, which must mean LSU is good, because A&M was a preseason top-5 team. Missouri was ranked in the preseason, for some reason, which must mean Mississippi State is also good, because they beat a preseason top-25 team. Obviously the preseason poll doesn't only affect one conference; Big Ten teams like Michigan, Penn State and Washington have looked far worse than preseason polls suggested. On the other hand, though, Nebraska and Wake Forest have received little attention and respect from voters, despite deserving it, because they didn't start the year in the top-25. Dawson continued, specifically calling out the SEC and how those teams fluctuate from week-to-week. "So we sit here and look at schedules, and obviously everything is SEC, SEC. Well look… they have all of their teams in the top-25. Guess what. Good for you. At the end of the year, half of them won’t be in the top-30. That’s just the way it is. We can’t sit here and say, ‘hey, we play X number of top-25 teams’. We don’t know that. We’ll count those chips up at the end of the year. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER "That’s why there shouldn’t be rankings, because you give people talking points that are idiots. They don’t know what they’re doing. Play the game. Play every week." It's like Dawson's been reading a certain OutKick writer's columns complaining about the polls each week. Ahem. Voters are humans, and humans are biased. They don't always watch all the games, and some have even forgotten to rank elite teams like Miami periodically. Some, like ESPN's Heather Dinich, post about the importance of winning "SEC road games," as if that some sort of remarkable achievement. Her specific example, Kentucky, beat a bad Texas A&M team and a bad South Carolina team. Great, so what? Why should that be rewarded by placing the Wildcats at No. 17, just because it's the SEC and those teams have big stadiums? OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD At the end of the day, using a blend of analytics and efficiency driven rankings would lead to a better result than trusting voters. Especially before anyone's even seen teams play on the field. But because there are vested interests who want preseason polls to continue, they will. Many valuable college football traditions have gone by the wayside in the modern game, but somehow not that one.

articles.title: Andy Robertson dismayed as Scotland 'outfought' by Slovenia in Nations League defeat
articles.summary: Scotland were "outfought" and simply "not good enough" in their 2-1 Nations League defeat by Slovenia, according to captain Andy Robertson.
articles.body:
Scotland were "outfought" and simply "not good enough" in their 2-1 Nations League defeat by Slovenia, says captain Andy Robertson.

Having won in North Macedonia on Saturday, Sebastien Pocognoli's side were favourites to back that up with another victory at Hampden Park.

The Scots led at half-time through Ryan Christie's close-range backheel, but were alarmingly open defensively and second-half goals from Danijel Sturm and Aljosa Matko turned the game on its head.

"Not good enough," Robertson told BBC Sport Scotland. "The whole team.

"We didn't do the good things we did on Saturday, I don't know what that's down to. They caused us a lot of problems and we have to find the reasons why.

Slovenia come from behind to beat ramshackle Scotland

Honeymoon over as Pocognoli's Scotland suffer domestic disharmony

How promotion, relegation and knockouts work in Nations League

"We wanted to kick on from Saturday because we had a really positive feeling about what we're doing and where we're going. We didn't do that.

"It's been a long camp, I don't know if it was down to tiredness, but Slovenia have played the same amount of games as us. They looked a lot fresher, more hungry.

"As Scotland, we might lack quality or make mistakes, but I don't think people accept being outfought. I think that's what happened tonight."

Pocognoli echoed his captain's assessment that Scotland were well below par.

"We didn't deserve to get the win, that's the reality," he said. "On the ball we were not clever enough. We were far from strong enough in the duels.

"The reality is each game teaches us some information. We will try to go through the process we want and learn from this one and do better in the next one."

Analysis: Pocognoli 'period of grace is over'

When Pocognoli took over as Steve Clarke's successor in August, the Belgian was clear he would try to take Scotland in a new direction.

He promised a more aggressive, more attacking style and called up several new faces - Josh McPake made his debut against Slovenia, following Stephen Welsh, Robbie Ure, Luis Binks and Luke Graham in the three previous fixtures.

Scotland should have won in Slovenia in Pocognoli's first match in charge, which ended in a goalless draw, before Jack Hendry's early red card hamstrung them in a 3-0 home defeat by Switzerland.

The win over North Macedonia was convincing and delivered a dose of optimism, but that has been severely dented and former Rangers midfielder Andy Halliday believes Pocognoli's honeymoon period is over already.

"I thought coming into this camp, Pocognoli would probably need a period of grace," Halliday said on Sportsound. "I think that period of grace is now over.

"That was as poor a Scotland performance as I can remember for a while against an opposition you are expecting us to go and beat."

Slovenia got in behind Scotland's high defensive line repeatedly and former national team captain Willie Miller is unsure if Pocognoli will stick with his back three.

"This is Pocognoli's preferred system and he's had time to work with the system, it was just all over the place," Miller said on Sportsound.

"Time and time again there were huge gaps appearing and Slovenia were taking advantage.

"Our situation is we've got a new manager in, he's got a preferred system, what does he do? Does he just bin it? Are we back to a back four?

"His preferred system is a back three, but it was unbelievably poor."

Send your views on the Scotland football team

articles.title: Scotland: Honeymoon over as Sebastien Pocognoli's side suffer domestic disharmony
articles.summary: Sebastien Pocognoli is left with questions to answer after an inert Scotland performance leaves him still searching for his first home win, writes Tom English.
articles.body:
On a dismal night at Hampden when Scotland failed to ask enough questions of Slovenia, there are one or two that could be posed to new boss Sebastien Pocognoli and his players.

We knew Pocognoli was a disciple of three at the back - the issue being whether he was rigid or flexible in his philosophy, whether he was a bit of an ideologue or a coach capable of changing things on the hoof.

Well, he changed it, that's for sure. Maybe not early as he should have, but at 1-1, and then when Slovenia took a deserved 2-1 lead, Pocognoli switched formation and personnel, not out of design but out of desperation, you felt.

He hurled players on in a bid to take a point; strikers, wingers, kitchen-sink stuff. Indiscriminate and messy. Scotland never really got out of the blocks. They got what they deserved.

So to the questions. Where did this turkey of a performance come from?

As early as the 13th minute there were signs of a rough night when Slovenia got in behind and Adam Cerin's shot had to be blocked by Jack Hendry. Concerning.

'Outfought' and 'not good enough' - Robertson on Scotland defeat

Slovenia come from behind to beat ramshackle Scotland at Hampden

How promotion, relegation and knockouts work in Nations League

It got a touch nervy as the visitors knocked it about, trying to work it into all the space that Scotland were affording them. Hampden was deathly quiet. Then Ryan Christie scored and it stirred, only to fall into a slumber again.

The trouble at the back was revisited soon after, Andy Roberton having to make a lung-busting effort to throw himself in front of a point-blank shot from Zan Vipotnik after Hendry was caught dozing.

The issues were obvious. Can the back three, so badly exposed by Slovenia, be long for this world when the opposition is decent? Why did all that acreage of space open out wide and through the middle? Slovenia were licking their lips for most of the night. They were clever and creative and should have won by more.

Why did Scotland's lauded midfield look so overrun? Seconds into the second half, Slovenia went straight through the middle again.

Was anybody taking note of the warning signs? Where was the intent and urgency? Where was the accuracy and the width? Where were the chances? Where were the bodies in the box supporting the frontman and the pressing game?

How could Slovenia go from being thoroughly outplayed by Scotland in the second half in Ljubljana to being so superior in Glasgow?

Aljosa Matko's equaliser started with a Scotland throw-in. Danijel Sturm's chance that should have made it 2-1 three minutes later came on the back of Ben Gannon-Doak staying miles up the pitch oblivious to Sturm's danger. Angus Gunn didn't exactly cover himself in glory, either.

The goal that we thought had made it 2-1 was disallowed - correctly - for offside, but the build-up was more of the same. Before Matko banged it past Gunn, Slovenia won one aerial duel and then another. Weak, weak, weak.

That second goal did come, as everybody suspected it would. Matko down the right, squared to Sturm. Easy. Luis Binks was caught this time. Soft, soft, soft.

Ramifications could stretch beyond this campaign

What does it all mean for Scotland's bid for second place in their Nations League group, a position that would give them a favourable pot two seeding for December's Euros draw?

That looks in jeopardy now. The ramifications of this defeat could stretch beyond the disappointment of a cold Tuesday night in Glasgow.

It was such a damaging evening for Pocognoli, a bolt from the blue, you sensed. He probably thought he was a little further down the road than he really is.

The air of dejection from him and his captain at the end was unmissable. It all sounded like some of the darker days under Steve Clarke.

There were giant empty spaces in the stands at Hampden but, at the end, there were enough fans left behind to deliver a lusty verdict on what they saw.

Going into this, there was positivity around Scotland's energy and the chances they'd been creating, about a burgeoning attacking style far removed from Clarke's supposed stodginess. All of that was badly undermined.

It wasn't so much that Scotland lost the game - bad enough in itself - it was how they lost. It was limp and lifeless for far too long.

Gannon-Doak played well as a wing-back last Saturday, but that was North Macedonia, not Slovenia. The youngster got targeted and exposed in a position he's not familiar with. Offensively, he was kept pretty quiet.

A back three that has looked impressive was hassled to distraction, calm replaced with confusion. Scotland's go-to leaders did not lead.

Robertson said his team was out-fought, which was a telling comment. Fight is the easiest part to get right, the thing that requires no talent.

On Saturday in Skopje, everything was easy for Scotland because North Macedonia were no good. They scored two and could have scored five and six.

Was there a sense of them believing in their own hype? Hard to imagine given that it was only North Macedonia they'd beaten, but there was a lack of edge about Scotland on Tuesday that begs that question.

Or can it all be laid at the door of the system? Slovenia did their work on that. Ripped it to pieces, in truth.

Pocognoli needs time, of course he does. He needs his most potent attacking midfielder, Scott McTominay, at the heart of things and needs more training sessions to drill his message into his players.

November is his next chance, away to Switzerland and home to North Macedonia. No real margin for error now. They had a big chance to make it a healthy seven points from four games and they blew it.

The head coach will need to nurse his wounds after this. He will have learned a lot about his players and has much thinking to do.

The honeymoon period is over. The reaction of the Hampden crowd at the end told you that the first marital row has now occurred.

articles.title: England: What has boss Thomas Tuchel learned during international break?
articles.summary: From Trent Alexander-Arnold's return to Alex Scott's debut, Phil McNulty assesses what England have learned during this international window.
articles.body:
England's World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina felt like the most painful wound of all as the so-called years of hurt stretched to six decades - but the process of recovery has started swiftly.

The extended international break and four Nations League games have afforded head coach Thomas Tuchel, so heavily criticised for his defensive tactics in that defeat in Atlanta, the opportunity to rebuild and rehabilitate from that disappointment.

Tuchel's squad included players recalled after being excluded from his plans and others who were new to the England fold, while mainstays like captain Harry Kane continued as the centrepiece of his plans.

So what has Tuchel learned from the start to England's Nations League campaign?

Kane inspires England to win over Czech Republic in Nations League

Kane scores twice but who else was a 'real threat'? England player ratings

Incomparable Kane leads unstoppable front four

There was a sense of inevitability that England captain Kane would be the star turn in Tuesday's 3-0 win over the Czech Republic as he celebrated equalling Peter Shilton's record of 125 England caps.

Kane, still irreplaceable at 33, added to his goals tally as England's all-time record scorer, his total of 91 now 38 ahead of Wayne Rooney, who is in second place in the listings with 53 goals in 120 games.

And, with Kane still looking in his prime and fully fit, it now seems only a matter of time before he makes history as the first player to score 100 goals for England.

This alone will have delighted Tuchel, but even more satisfying for the German is that he now presides over an attacking quartet that can pose a threat to any side in world football.

Kane is the peerless spearhead, but Anthony Gordon - on target in the three Nations League games against Spain, the Czech Republic and Croatia before being rested here at Wembley - has moved his game on to another level since joining Barcelona from Newcastle.

Gordon is a creator with burning pace, while on the right flank Bukayo Saka has looked rejuvenated after a World Cup during which he was hampered by an Achilles injury, as he proved with two goals in Croatia.

And, just behind them all, with everything he does stamped with world class, is Jude Bellingham, England's player of the year and the golden future of his country at only 23.

This may be bad news for Chelsea's Cole Palmer, whose withdrawal from England's squad has allowed others to cement their place in front of him, with Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White proving his commitment by cutting short a family holiday to join the squad after being excluded initially.

England's front four looks a natural fit, augmented by Chelsea's Morgan Rogers, while Liverpool's 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha will be an international contender for years to come.

If Tuchel can keep his fab four fit and firing, England will be a danger to any opponents.

Kane's rise from childhood keeper to equalling England cap record

England's greatest international? Kane is now a serious contender

In a camp of positives, a major disappointment for England and Tuchel was the injury suffered by Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott after an outstanding debut in the 7-0 win in Croatia.

Scott slipped seamlessly into England's midfield with powerful running, a complete range of passing and an energy to his link play that made the 23-year-old look perfectly at home at international level.

Scott's emergence showed the array of riches Tuchel has at his disposal in the central midfield area, even with Arsenal's Declan Rice, a fixture in the team, out as his load is managed after injury.

Indeed, Scott was so impressive that Tuchel said: "Is Declan still for me a fixed point in my team? Yes, but some other players are coming and impressing and it's an ongoing competition."

It was hardly a shot across Rice's bows, but certainly an indication of the options available to England.

So the thigh injury that ruled him out against the Czech Republic was a blow to Scott and England - as well as Bournemouth, who fear he will be sidelined for two months.

Elliot Anderson, Manchester City's £116m summer purchase from Nottingham Forest, also goes from strength to strength after a good World Cup, while Tuchel was prepared to give Arsenal's 20-year-old Myles Lewis-Skelly his head in central midfield in these Nations League games.

Everton's James Garner has also figured and has a big admirer in Tuchel, even referring to him as England's "mini Valverde" - a somewhat tongue-in-cheek reference to Real Madrid midfielder Federico perhaps, but a sign of how highly he is rated.

Manchester United's Kobbie Mainoo pulled out injured while Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton, so highly-rated, has been unable to force his way into Tuchel's plans.

Alexander-Arnold is back - and should be back for good

Tuchel's treatment of Trent Alexander-Arnold had provided a constant backdrop to his time as England head coach, with what appeared to be his mistrust of the Real Madrid right-back's defensive frailties culminating in his exclusion from the World Cup squad.

Alexander-Arnold's card looked marked from the moment Tuchel, after leaving him out of World Cup qualifiers against Andorra and Serbia in August 2025, said: "If he wants to have this impact in the English national team then he has to take the defensive part very, very seriously.

"Because when we are talking, especially about qualifying football, and then tournament football, the one defensive error, the one moment where you are not 100% awake, can be decisive. It can be the moment where you pack your suitcases and go home."

Tuchel, however, appeared to set those reservations to one side when he recalled him for these four Nations League games - and Alexander-Arnold responded with performances that simply demand his continued inclusion.

The 27-year-old made his first start under Tuchel - in fact his first since scoring in the Nations League win in Finland in October 2024 - against the Czech Republic in Prague, demonstrating the extra dimension he offers England with a world-class cross for Gordon's opener.

Alexander-Arnold was a potent force once more against the Czechs at Wembley, forcing a fine early save from keeper Lukas Hornicek with a 30-yard free-kick then providing several more trademark dangerous crosses.

True, any potential defensive deficiencies were not probed, but Alexander-Arnold showed enough class and creation to surely avoid being discarded again by Tuchel.

Newcastle United's Lewis Hall emerged as one of the big winners from England's opening round of Nations League matches, making a strong case to become Tuchel's long-term left-back.

Hall stepped in for three matches after Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly, first choice at the World Cup and for the opening game against Spain, returned to his club with an injury.

It allowed Hall, who has just signed a new contract tying him to Newcastle until 2031, the opportunity to stake his claim - and he did so in style.

The 22-year-old impressed in both games against Czech Republic and also in the rout in Croatia, with one key factor sure to play out in his favour.

Hall's left-flank partnership with former Newcastle United team-mate Gordon looked a natural fit, the pair working in tandem to perfection in a manner that will give Tuchel serious food for thought.

O'Reilly has done nothing wrong, but questions remain as to whether he is a natural left-back or simply a converted midfield player.

Hall looked the part in every respect. He has made it difficult for Tuchel to leave him out, the link with Gordon only adding to the attraction for England's head coach.

articles.title: Harry Kane breaks England appearance record but can he take that final step to complete his career?
articles.summary: Harry Kane got two goals and an assist on his 125th cap for England in the 3-0 win over the Czech Republic; the England captain is now level with Peter Shilton at the top of the Three Lions' all-time appearance list - but Kane still needs that trophy to be the undisputed best
articles.body:
On his 125th cap, Kane did what Kane does best under the Wembley arch - stealing the show, leading the way, winning the game for England.

Everyone knew he would score in this match. It's the same feeling you get in every match. But he still gets the buzz.

"I think this is even beyond my wildest dreams," he said after the game. "To be now at 125, it's just an extreme privilege."

This match - and the three goals he contributed to England's cause on his special night - was a perfect summary of Harry Kane's England career.

The first goal saw him venture out to the right wing, highlighting Kane's ability to pop up anywhere on the pitch. Quarterback, out wide, it doesn't matter. It's classic Kane.

But his two goals were classic centre-forward strikes. Right in the heart of the penalty area, almost a throwback to the classic No 9.

"He's playing at a level that is unmatched," said Jude Bellingham on Kane's record-breaking night. "He's scoring goals for fun, he's dropping deep and playing passes in behind and contributing, making tackles and everything. He's only getting better."

What makes Kane's achievement even more incredible is he has reached 125 caps despite making his England debut at 21. For a generational talent in the modern game, that's somewhat rare. Bellingham, for example, was 17 when he played his first game.

Kane did not have the teenage sensation moment Wayne Rooney or Micheal Owen had. Bukayo Saka and Rio Ferdinand were also 19 on their England debuts. Declan Rice and Phil Foden were 20. Kane was the slow starter who forged his way up through the EFL and became a national hero.

And what has followed is 125 caps in 11 years. The remarkable consistency is summarised by his availability. He's always there for England.

In England's last 101 competitive matches - which spans a decade - Kane has been available for selection for all but one of them: the Nations League loss to Greece in 2024.

Every single other game, he has been able to be called upon for the Three Lions. A century of near-perfectly consistent England performances over the span of a decade.

"For sure there's times I've played through the pain", he said. "I think every player at some stage plays through the pain or niggles or some sort of injury.

"I think the last six years or so I've been extremely consistent in that sense and been available. I think availability is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level."

Now it's important to recognise that Kane hasn't always been 100 per cent fit in those 100 matches. The Euro 2024 campaign and final spring to mind where he was clearly carrying something but playing through the pain.

But his predecessor at the England elite level in Rooney was riddled with injury sagas through his career - Euro 2004 and the 2006 World Cup especially.

The main image of his 2010 World Cup highlight reel was him shouting down the TV cameras to England fans, then he faded out of form in 2012, 2014 and 2016 - to the point where he was no longer the main man. Kane has shown the consistency Rooney never could.

Now Rooney, Owen and Co were part of a different generation where playing for England was not as attractive as it is now. Turning up regularly for international duty was not as common, with the 'club first culture' well-documented on many levels.

But then again, Kane's big night came on the same evening that Cristiano Ronaldo revealed his reasons for leaving the Portugal camp. Even the very best can easily turn away from the national team for any reason. Kane has never even given a glimmer of that attitude in his 11 years.

"To reach the highest level on a consistent basis you've always got to be hungry, you've always got to be striving for more," he said.

"I think sometimes players or people can reach the top and think it's time to take their foot off the gas and that's when you see players maybe fall.

"For me it's the opposite. When I'm at the top it's to do even more, find even more improvement. That's what I'm doing right now."

Kane is the exemplary player England needed for this generation - but all that remains is for him to confirm his place as the greatest player in any generation.

Is he already England's best? Quite possibly. Record appearance maker and goalscorer is hard to top and argue against. But the one thing Ronaldo, Bobby Charlton and Bobby Moore have over him is silverware at international level. "For sure I'd swap all [the caps and goals] to win something with England."

But Kane also said: "Every player has a ceiling." What is his? Has he already reached it? "I hope not. I hope there's still more to go. I guess only time dictates that, where everyone's ceiling is.

"Right now I still feel like I've got room to improve. I just said that I've come off the back of my best season ever at 32 years old and right now I feel even in a better place."

There is still plenty for him to get. Kane is first eyeing up 100 goals at international level, joining a very elite club of strikers to manage that feat. He will surely get there.

"I try not to think about it too much," he said, with a sense of humility. "It's like being a cricketer in the 90s, the more you think about the 100, you don't know where to get there.

But in this all-time great innings - as well as the upcoming Ballon D'Or trophy, which he surely has more than half a chance for - delivering a first major international trophy since 1966 is the ultimate prize.

Kane has at least one more bite at the trophy cherry. He looks set to appear at Euro 2028 and possibly he can squeeze out one last crack at the World Cup, following this summer's disappointment.

"I'm in great shape," he said. "Some of the players I've played with went into their late 30s and are still at the highest level and are even in their 40s now. It's season by season with me.

"As long as I feel like I can help the team and be valuable for the team I'll be around. At the moment I feel like I can't help the team, I won't and that's the way I am. We'll have to see."

For now, one message stands with Kane. "Don't give yourself any regrets." He has done so much - but it's time for the last, big challenge. Win it all. Win what remains.

articles.title: JJ Gabriel: Man Utd prodigy yet to make decision on future amid interest from Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and PSG
articles.summary: Sky Sports News understands JJ Gabriel and his family are yet to make a decision on his future; Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and PSG all interested; it is likely Gabriel's next club is in Europe; United could consider legal action if he moves to a European club
articles.body:
Real Madrid and Barcelona retain a strong interest, while Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich continue to keep a close eye on his situation.

Gabriel turned 16 on Tuesday, which is the age at which European clubs are allowed to sign him to a professional contract.

Gabriel is eligible to apply for a European passport through his parents.

Sky Sports News reported on Monday evening that United will consider legal action if he moves to a European club.

However, it is understood that this is not a concern to Gabriel and his camp as they consider their next move for the 16-year-old.

Gabriel was pictured in United's squad photo for the 2026/27 season on Monday but is still expected to leave Old Trafford.

Sky Sports News understands the picture was taken on September 8, when Gabriel was still at the club and expected to feature for the first team this season.

It was just days later that Gabriel and his family put in a formal request to leave.

Gabriel remains registered with United and Sky Sports News understands multiple attempts have been made to reconcile the situation with the 16-year-old and his family, with duty of care being a factor for such a young player, but no progress has been made.

Gabriel has attracted the interest of Europe's biggest clubs and talks have taken place between his camp and the likes of Barcelona and Real Madrid, with PSG and Bayern Munich also interested in the young attacking talent.

From United's perspective, they feel they have done all they can to show Gabriel and his family a clear pathway to their first team while also protecting his long-term development.

This involves, for example, featuring in the first-team squad photo that was released on Monday - a message he was to be involved in Michael Carrick's plans this season.

Another action they would point to is having Gabriel train with the first team for pre-season while also making his debut against Atletico Madrid in a friendly during that time.

However, Gabriel and his family would point to wanting more than the eight to nine minutes off the bench that he got in that particular game.

Gabriel's involvement in pre-season came after the then 15-year-old failed to report back with the academy squad at the beginning of pre-season as expected.

The U21s arrived back at Carrington a week before the first team, and Gabriel was due back at the same time.

But his family believed it was beneath him and were of the view he should only be involved in first-team training and so pulled him out of reporting back with the U21s.

Sky Sports News also understands Gabriel had an individual development plan led by first-team coaches at the club, including the first-team's medical and performance departments - who all engaged with Gabriel and his family to ensure he was receiving the attention they felt he deserved.

However, despite there being a feeling from inside the club the relationship between them and Gabriel's camp was harmonious, there was a difference of opinion over how much he would feature for the first team at the beginning of the season.

Gabriel and his family requested he feature for at least 20 minutes against Sabah in the Champions League, Brighton in the FA Cup and Bournemouth in the Premier League on October 25. This was all before beginning negotiations around a scholarship contract to secure his future at the club.

Gabriel was ineligible for the first-team tie against Sabah as he was not put in United's A-list. Instead, he played against the Azerbaijani side in the UEFA Youth League that day and scored a hat-trick.

Now that Gabriel has turned 16, he would automatically be added to the club's B-list and would be eligible for matchday squads going forward - but Gabriel's family will believe that was the opportune moment for him to be involved in first-team action.

As previously reported, despite being registered until the end of the season, there is a belief that due to a FIFA loophole, Gabriel could leave United for a club in Europe after his 16th birthday if he obtains a European passport, which he could through either of his parents.

Gabriel has not trained with United since.

Club sources believe the tension between the two camps stems from Gabriel's family wanting to chase historical records and United wanting to protect his long-term development.

To this point, no club-to-club contact has been made regarding the availability of Gabriel.

Sky Sports News has been told that if a European club tries to lure him away through a FIFA loophole, United will consider legal action.

It is presumed from the club's perspective that the change in attitude from Gabriel's family around the Sabah game revolves around promises made from elsewhere - whether from another European club or potential representation acting on Gabriel and his family's behalf.

For now the teenager remains a United player and despite the fractured relationship, those at the club still believe they are the best place for Gabriel and his individual development.

However, it remains unlikely we will ever see Gabriel in a United shirt again, with Europe's biggest clubs circling the young star.

articles.title: Luka Modric y el secreto de la eterna juventud: "Mientras me sienta así, quiero seguir jugando"
articles.standfirst: No pone fecha de caducidad a su final, mientras ve como leyendas como Messi ya se despiden de su selección.
articles.summary: No pone fecha de caducidad a su final, mientras ve como leyendas como Messi ya se despiden de su selección.
articles.body: El tiempo no castiga a todos por igual. Hay quien consigue que los años sean experiencia, conocimiento, madurez, pero no vejez. Es un arte que pocos dominan y los que lo hacen no comparten el secreto porque para ellos es algo natural. Banalizan situaciones extraordinarias y alargan su leyenda muy por encima de lo que cualquiera podría esperar. Que se lo digan a Luka Modric, que con 41 años no parece querer negociar consigo mismo el adiós al fútbol: "Me siento bien. Sigo teniendo pasión, ambición y fuerza. Mientras me sienta así, quiero seguir jugando. ¿Cuánto será? No lo sé. Pueden ser dos meses, seis meses, un año... No quiero decir algo ahora y luego arrepentirme. Voy a ir poco a poco, partido a partido. Un mes, otro mes... Tengo que escuchar a mi cuerpo y luego decidiré con total tranquilidad. Veremos si este es mi último año o sigo más, pero me siento bien". Es indiscutible. Se siente bien y lo demuestra cada vez que juega al fútbol. Cuando el croata mira atrás sólo puede sentirse orgulloso. Más allá de los éxitos deportivos, se ha ganado el respeto de sus aficionados, como era de esperar, pero también de los rivales, como el otro día en el Pizjuán. "El homenaje en España no me lo esperaba. Me quedé muy agradecido a los aficionados de Sevilla. Sé que mucha gente me quiere. Recibir esa ovación en un partido internacional es increíble. Me quedé sin palabras", reconoce con cierta vergüenza. El final de Modric se acerca y con él se cerrará el mejor capítulo de la historia del fútbol croata. Una generación de la que aún quedan supervivientes. "Cada vez me queda menos de esa selección. A Perisic, a mí, a Budimir, a Kramaric o a mí no nos queda mucho. A Kovacic lo quieren meter en ese saco, pero tiene mucho futuro por delante. Espero que los que vienen sigan haciendo cosas grandes. Yo estoy orgulloso de todo lo que he hecho y de todo lo que he conseguido con la selección", reconoce. El tramo final de la carrera de Modric coincide con el de otras leyendas del fútbol. Messi se despide de Argentina, Cristiano está en crisis en Portugal... Ellos fueron sus compañeros de batallas y sus rivales más complicados. "¿Qué decir de Messi? Es una pena que se despida de su selección, pero es su decisión y hay que respetarlo. Ganó el Mundial que quería, es uno de los mejores jugadores del mundo y ha sido un placer verlo jugar, aunque lo he sufrido mucho con la selección y con el Madrid. Es un jugador único. Le deseo mucha suerte". Bien distinta es la situación que vive su amigo y excompañero Cristiano Ronaldo, que sigue en guerra con Portugal. "No he hablado con él y no sé exactamente qué ha pasado. Es una pena lo que está pasando con él en su país, pero creo que van a encontrar una solución. Cris se lo merece. Si no va a seguir merece una despedida a lo grande. Espero que se solucione porque es el jugador más grande de Portugal", aseguraba Luka. Modric sigue rindiendo en el AC Milan y con su selección, pero con el ocaso asomando todos imaginan un posible regreso al Real Madrid. "Claro que me gustaría volver. Es mi casa. Es el club de mi vida. He estado 13 años ahí, pero veremos qué pasa en el futuro. Me tengo que preparar y tengo que ver en qué función puedo ayudar o si el club quiere. Se tienen que dar muchas cosas para volver, sería un sueño, pero de momento no pienso en ello. No debemos forzar nada. Tiene que ser algo en lo que me sienta útil". Él, por lo que pueda pasar, no quita ojo a lo que sucede en Valdebebas y mantiene contacto con la gente de allí. "A Mourinho le dije que está en el club que merece estar porque es uno de los más grandes. Hablo con muchos jugadores y gente del club. Creo que el Madrid tiene un equipazo y puede dar la vuelta a la situación. El Madrid tiene carácter y calidad. Tienen todo lo que necesitan para cambiar la situación. Yo echo de menos Madrid, pero ahora sigo disfrutando en Milán. Me recibieron muy bien e intento dar el máximo", confesaba.
