articles.title: High School Football: Dunbar set to play varsity games on back-to-back days
articles.summary: The Dunbar High School football program is pulling double duty this week in an effort to make up a previously canceled game. The Wolverines will be playing v...
articles.body:
The Dunbar High School football program is pulling double duty this week in an effort to make up a previously canceled game.

The Wolverines will be playing varsity football games on back-to-back days. Dunbar is playing Cincinnati Northwest (6-1) at 6 p.m. on Thurs., Oct. 8. The next day, Dunbar will face Stivers (0-4) at 7 p.m. Both games will be held at Welcome Stadium.

Dunbar athletic director Deondra Wynn confirmed Tuesday that both games will be played.

Dunbar was originally set to play Stivers on Aug. 28. It was canceled a few days after Dayton Public School officials canceled the Stivers football season. DPS ended up restarting the Stivers season two days later.

High school football: Mississinawa Valley superintendent backs coach who resigned after bullying investigation

The Wolverines will be playing three games in a seven-day span. The game against Northwest will be held on five days rest for Dunbar. The team lost to Trotwood 51-6 in its most recent game on Friday, Oct. 2.

The Dayton Daily News has reached out to Ohio High School Athletic Association officials for comment.

OHSAA regulations allow for a maximum of four quarters to played in one day, per regulation 1.31. There are no regulations regarding playing games on consecutive days or requiring a designated rest period in-between games. In season practice regulation 1.18.1 reads "consider limiting full contact on consecutive days."

In its final two scheduled games of the season, Dunbar will play Thurgood Marshall on Oct. 17 and Meadowdale on Oct. 22.

Dunbar is 3-3 overall this season and are in first-place in the Dayton City League standings with a 2-0 record.
authors: Steven Wright, Dayton Daily News, Ohio

articles.title: Bengals still seeking identity on offense amid run-game woes
articles.summary: CINCINNATI — The Cincinnati Bengals realized early on in their loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, Oct. 4, that the running game wasn’t getting them...
articles.body:
CINCINNATI — The Cincinnati Bengals realized early on in their loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, Oct. 4, that the running game wasn't getting them anywhere.

Joe Burrow's response to that was "let's throw it more," and that's what they did, but coaches and players since then have acknowledged it's not a sustainable way to win games. The Bengals are still establishing their identity on offense but look for solutions to bounce back this week as they prepare to face the Miami Dolphins (0-4) on the road Sunday.

Burrow threw 54 passes and completed 39 of them for 428 yards and one touchdown, but had two interceptions and a third that was negated by a late hit. Three impressive completions to begin the final drive gave the Bengals a chance to win, but ultimately, a pass to Chase Brown fell inches short of a first down in the red zone with 50 seconds left.

The Bengals finished with 15 carries for 23 yards, fell 22-17 to the Jaguars and are 2-2 heading into the final game before the bye.

"It just wasn't good enough," Bengals coach Zac Taylor said. "That falls on all of us to be better at it. Is it a dramatic shift? No. It's not a dramatic shift. But there are things that we can continue to work in and that will fit us. Part of, through four weeks, you're finding what your identity is going to be for the whole year. I think, first quarter of the season, you got a snapshot of OK, here are some things that we can continue to emphasize. Here are some things that we need. And so we have to improve at them — we can't just abandon them — and find what our identity is going to be these last three quarters of the season. … We'll be smart enough to adjust and do what's best for our offense to score points."

Cincinnati Bengals: Chase, Higgins remain 'day-to-day'

The Bengals had been efficient — but not explosive — in the running game the first three games, but Brown managed just 10 yards on nine carries and 71 yards receiving on 11 catches, which tied Tee Higgins for the most receptions in the game.

Jacksonville finished with 111 yards rushing on 27 carries (4.1 yards per carry).

"I think we got to do a better job with communication," Bengals center Ted Karras said when asked how to fix the running game. "That starts with me up front. I think that game just declared to what it was, you know, turning into a 400-yard passing game. What we communicated to the guys today, we did have a chance to win at the end, and that would have maybe covered up some of this stuff, but as a unit, we felt that this was well below our standard, and we need to get better."

Karras said the offensive line's performance overall wasn't good enough, and it reminded him of last year's blowout loss at Minnesota when the Bengals managed just 171 yards of offense and Jake Browning was pressured 17 times.

Cincinnati moved the ball better than that on Sunday, but a team that passes for 428 yards should be able to score more than 17 points, Karras said. Burrow was pressured 14 times and sacked twice, with those being charged to Dalton Risner and Amarius Mims, according to Pro Football Focus.

"I didn't think we passed off stunts very well," Karras said. "I think we gave up way too many hits. I think everyone took a turn doing something that equated to 17 points, which isn't going to get it done. I think our defense gave us a winning effort – 22 points against the Jags should come out of there with a win, and ultimately ended up coming, what six inches short on fourth and 10? It wasn't our best."

Archdeacon: 'This was our time to make a play'

Taylor said when you're passing more than 50 times, protection is going to be an issue. Risner was playing on an injured knee, and the Jaguars have a strong defensive line that made it even more challenging.

Cleaning up the run game to take pressure off the offensive line and quarterback will be key going forward. Offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher said that's going to take a combination of the players better understanding their responsibilities, executing and making better in-game decisions and the coaches making decisions in-game and evaluating the best way to move forward at any given point in the season.

"I don't think the way we played the game yesterday is a sustainable strategy for long-term success," Pitcher said. "I do think we chose to play the game (Sunday) in a way that gave us the best chance to win (Sunday). We need to look at what we're doing well and, more importantly, what we're not doing well, and set us on a course to get better."

Karras said going from 2-0 to open the season to now sitting at 2-2 "doesn't feel very good" but the Bengals must get to 3-2 going into the bye. A quarter of the way through the season, it's time to establish what kind of team this is going to be for the rest of the season.

"September football's over, so it's going to start declaring who we are, and I love what Pitch said at the beginning of the year: We can be whoever we need to be to win a football game," Karras said. "Had a chance airing it out. Obviously, we have the best QB and receivers in the world. So now we just have to keep running. Got to get back to practice, and we got to go to South Florida and get a win before the bye."

articles.title: After QB switch in win over Auburn, No. 15 Tennessee set to start George MacIntyre against Arkansas
articles.summary: MacIntyre replaced Faizon Brandon late in the first half of the 24-14 win.
articles.body:
Tennessee is sticking with the quarterback change it made midway through its win over Auburn in Week 5.

According to multiple reports, George MacIntyre will start against Arkansas on Saturday. MacIntyre replaced Faizon Brandon during the No. 15 Vols' 24-14 Week 5 win .

The sophomore came on at the end of the first half after Brandon was 3-of-8 passing for zero yards and an interception. Tennessee punted on its first four drives of the game — and ran 16 plays over those four drives — as Brandon's first completion went for seven yards and his next two then lost seven yards.

MacIntyre finished the game 8-of-10 passing for 86 yards. Tennessee's offense was powered by 34 carries for 220 yards and three touchdowns by running back DeSean Bishop.

Brandon won the team's quarterback competition in fall camp as the Vols needed to replace starting QB Joey Aguilar. The interception he threw against Auburn was his first of the season, but he had failed to crack 200 yards passing in each of Tennessee's last three games.

Against No. 1 Texas in Week 4, Brandon was 17-of-29 passing for 145 yards and a TD. He was also sacked 10 times as Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons had 5.5 of those sacks.

A Nashville native, MacIntyre was a four-star recruit in the class of 2025 and the No. 4 prospect in the state of Tennessee. He was ranked as the No. 16 quarterback in the country in the class ahead of players like Pitt's Mason Heintschel and BYU's Bear Bachmeier.

articles.title: Ex-49ers DB urges team to trade for Pro Bowl DT
articles.summary: The 49ers need defensive line help and could find a key piece with a potential trade for an 0-4 team.
articles.body:
Richard Sherman thinks the San Francisco 49ers should revisit a trade for Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea.

The former 49ers cornerback made his pitch on the "Richard Sherman Podcast" after San Francisco's Week 4 win over the Denver Broncos .

"If I'm [49ers general manager] John Lynch, I'm calling the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and saying, 'Hey, he was disgruntled before, you guys weren't sellers, you're 0-4 right now, are you sellers or not? What is the price?' And if the price isn't above a third-rounder, then I think you got to make that move," Sherman said. "Even if it's just a one-season rental, I think you got to make that move and try to get this team better, especially against the run. I mean, it only strengthens your team. He's one of the best defensive tackles in the National Football League."

San Francisco did call about Vea in August, though. NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported the 49ers were among the teams that inquired after Vea requested a trade at the start of training camp. But on Aug. 19, V ea and the Buccaneers agreed to a one-year extension worth $30 million . The deal keeps him in Tampa Bay through 2027 and includes $6 million in new money this year.

Vea, who's from nine miles north of Santa Clara, California, is 31 and a two-time Pro Bowler. He had 51 pressures last season, tied for seventh among interior defensive linemen, according to Pro Football Focus. This season, he has just eight combined tackles through four games.

San Francisco's need up front is clear. Nick Bosa is out with a calf and knee issue and is expected to miss multiple weeks and James Thompson Jr. is out with an ankle injury; Keion White (hamstring) and Romello Height (hand) are also banged up. Sam Okuayinonu, Alfred Collins, C.J. West and Mikail Kamara are on injured reserve. Mykel Williams could return soon after his 21-day practice window opened following his 2025 ACL injury, but there's no guarantee he'll look good immediately.

Vea would fill a huge need to bolster the defensive line, but it's unclear if the 49ers are in a position to make a move. They traded a third-round pick for Osa Odighizuwa this past offseason, who has seven combined tackles and five quarterback hits this season.

articles.title: 📹 Vintage Messi shines in emotional Argentina farewell
articles.summary: At a packed Monumental de Núñez in Buenos Aires, Lionel Andrés Messi Cuccittini bid farewell to Argentina's national team with a 3–0 win over Benin in a frie...
articles.body:
At a packed Monumental de Núñez in Buenos Aires, Lionel Andrés Messi Cuccittini bid farewell to Argentina's national team with a 3–0 win over Benin in a friendly that wrapped up the October international window on Tuesday (6).

The result certainly isn't what matters most.

Even if it does help boost Messi's stats for the Albiceleste even further.

After all, the star in the No. 10 shirt provided the assists for Otamendi and Nico Paz's goals, as well as scoring one himself.

Those goals, incidentally, all came in the second half and, in a way, reflected Messi's more than 20 years in an Argentina shirt.

Otamendi's goal, for example—he was also bidding farewell to the Albiceleste—came from a Messi corner that the defender turned into the net. A classic, right?

And the young Argentine gem's goal came in the genius's signature style: a well-placed left-footed shot from the edge of the box that gave the goalkeeper no chance. The classic "passing of the torch."

How many times have we seen Messi score goals like that for Barcelona, PSG, Inter Miami and, of course, the three-time world champions?

Finally, from the penalty spot, the genius in the No. 10 shirt sent the goalkeeper the wrong way and fired into the top corner, bringing his beautiful story in an Argentina shirt to a close with absolute class.

With his final touch of the ball for Argentina, Messi took a free kick from the edge of the box, as he had so many times in his career, but this time it went over the crossbar.

Messi thus bids farewell to Argentina's national team with 126 goals (26 of them penalties) and 70 assists in 208 official appearances.

With the Albiceleste, the genius in the No. 10 shirt won the 2022 World Cup, the 2021 and 2024 Copa América titles, and the 2022 Finalissima.

Across his professional career, Lionel Messi now has 932 goals and, at 39, is still going strong in pursuit of 1,000 goals!

🥹 Emotions running high long before kickoff

Buenos Aires, Rosario and all of Argentina came to a standstill to honor Lionel Messi.

The genius in the No. 10 shirt tried his hardest to hold back his tears during Argentina's national anthem.

Coach Lionel Scaloni, known as a "real softie," was overcome with emotion during the Argentine anthem.

Benin's national team, which had the honor of taking part in the farewell celebrations, presented Messi with a small statue and a letter.

Ten minutes into the match, the friendly was paused for more celebrations in honor of Lionel Messi.

articles.title: El 'dios' Messi se despide de Argentina con un gol y dos asistencias
articles.standfirst: El 10 se va siendo, como siempre, el mejor de la Albiceleste ante una Benín digna
articles.summary: El 10 se va siendo, como siempre, el mejor de la Albiceleste ante una Benín digna
articles.body: Leo Messi ya es historia de la Selección argentina. Una historia con un último capítulo emocionante, el de esta noche en el Mas Monumental de Buenos Aires. Un capítulo coronado con dos asistencias y un gol (de penalti) del astro para el 3-0 de la Albiceleste ante la digna Benín. La historia puso fin así una película de ensueño para Argentina, una película que empezó aquel 17 de agosto de 2005 con un partido ante Hungría. 208 partidos después y 126 goles más tarde, Leo Messi dijo adiós a la Selección con este emotivo amistoso contra Benín (un rival impropio por nombre, considerando quién se despedía, aunque muy digno en su actuación). Lo cierto es que la primera parte tuvo un protagonismo inesperado de Benín, la Selección 89 del ránking FIFA (de 211 países), y que le puso dignidad al fútbol plantándole cara a Argentina. Lo hicieron muy bien los africanos. Sorprendieron a todos los que esperaban una goleada desde el minuto 1. Una cosa no cambió: casi todo el peligro en el primer acto lo protagonizó LM. Un disparo desde fuera del área; una falta directa; un remate de volea; todos con marchamo de gol, pero ninguno entró por la buena actuación del portero rival, Marcel Dandjinou, que ya en la previa del partido nos decía en MARCA que su trabajo "no era regalarle nada a Messi". Y lo cumplió. La segunda parte fue más lógica, con la asistencia número 69 del astro Leo. Fue en un córner y lo remató Nico Otamendi, el otro que se despedía de la Albiceleste (fue cambiado minutos después). Una jugada que representó el (ya) pasado de esta gloriosa Selección. Poco después llegó el golazo de Nico Paz (2-0) tras la segunda asistencia (ésta más tímida) de un Leo Messi que mira al jugador nacido en España (Tenerife) como uno de sus posibles sucesores, al menos en cuanto al dorsal se refiere. Fue un golazo, ésa es la verdad. El 3-0 sí fue de Leo, en un penalti clamoroso hecho sobre Giay. Leo agarró la pelota y anotó su diana número 126 con la Albiceleste. Ya estaba todo hecho... si había aún algo por hacer para este 'extraterrestre' del balón. En el 74', eso sí, Leo falló lo increíble en un pase a la red que le salió a un lado. Hubiera sido la guinda con el 4-0 que no llegó... y a punto estuvo de hacerlo también en el 89' con un remate al palo de Leo. Y así se fue el partido, esperando el momento en el que Leo iba a ser sustituido para vivir sus últimos segundos de esta historia de éxitos y dificultades (que también las hubo) de Leo con su Selección nacional. Messi no fue sustituido, jugó los 90'... y ahí se apagó su luz, pero nace su leyenda. Una leyenda fantástica del más grande de la historia de este deporte.

articles.title: Lionel Messi Scores in Final Match with Argentina, Top Moments, Highlights and Reaction
articles.summary: It's only fitting that Lionel Messi is going out a winner with a brilliant individual performance.
articles.body:
It's only fitting that Lionel Messi is going out a winner with a brilliant individual performance.

The soccer legend played his final international game for Argentina on Tuesday and led his side to a 3-0 win over Benin in a friendly at Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires with a goal and two assists.

His assists started the scoring in the second half, while his goal came on a penalty kick and provided some insurance for the victors.

The actual game took a backseat to the celebration of an iconic career, as the 39-year-old's resume with his nation includes the 2022 World Cup championship, three World Cup final appearances, two Copa América titles and 126 goals over the course of 21 years.

Tuesday's game was always going to be a spectacle given Messi's overall importance to Argentina and the sport of soccer as a whole.

He even revealed leading up to the contest he was going to wear a jersey with gold numbers, writing, "Último partido… Una camiseta para toda la vida ❤️One last match… A jersey for a lifetime," on Instagram .

It was an emotional scene before the game kicked off, as Messi walked out with his children and had tears in his eyes during the national anthem. Benin captain Sessi D'Almeida also gave him a gift prior to the coin toss.

Benin players were also among those who recognized No. 10's greatness when the match was paused in the 10th minute:

The crowd was anxious for a memorable moment in the game as well, but Benin goalkeeper Marcel Dandjinou had other ideas in the early going. He saved all four of Argentina's shots on goal in the first half and preserved a scoreless tie into intermission.

Messi was aggressive with four shots himself in the first half, but none of them found the back of the net despite all the fanfare.

It was just a matter of time before someone scored for Argentina, though, and Nicolás Otamendi buried a shot off Messi's corner kick. It wasn't a goal for the legend, but he tallied the assist on a perfectly placed cross.

Messi assisted Argentina's second goal as well when Nico Paz took his pass and connected on a left-footed shot from outside the box.

But the fans wanted to see a Messi goal as well, and they finally got it in the 71st minute on a penalty strike.

All that was left to do from there was celebrate his greatness, which is something Argentina fans have grown accustomed to throughout his career.
